boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Spotsylvania Court House record (May 8-21, 1864) in Grant's Overland Campaign [May-June 1864]. The Wilderness (VA046) ends on May 7; Yellow Tavern (VA052, May 11) is a separate cavalry record fought near Richmond within these dates, and the North Anna (VA055) begins on May 23. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live force fields read 152,000 (US 100,000; CS 52,000). Humphreys relays Early's statement that Hill's corps had about 13,000 muskets for duty when he took command on May 8, Ewell's that his corps barely numbered 8,000 after losing Johnson's division on the 12th, and Ewell's 6,000 at Harris Farm on the 19th. For Union reinforcements he gives Hancock's 8,000 with Tyler, a regiment of 1,500, and an effective force sent between May 4 and June 12 of probably about 12,000; Upton's brigade was 'now only 800 strong' on the 14th.
claims.rationale: Partial, secondhand figures for different dates, formations and populations; reinforcements are not opening strength. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive (Grant continued his offensive); the live result reads Indecisive. Meade says the May 12 assault took Johnson and Steuart with over 3,000 prisoners and 20 guns; Humphreys relays Hancock's nearly 4,000 prisoners and twenty guns. Meade says the enemy retired to an inner line on the 13th; NPS says Grant disengaged on May 21 and continued toward Richmond.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Meade's and Hancock's prisoner counts differ and are not reconciled.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 30,000 (US 18,000; CS 12,000); the live field reads 27,000 (US 18,000; CS 9,000). Humphreys gives the Army of the Potomac, May 8–19, 1,411 missing and 14,679 total, and with Burnside's figures 15,722 killed and wounded, 2,001 missing and 17,723 in all; he reports Badeau's 13,601 as too small. He has no accurate Confederate account, puts their May 12 loss at between 9,000 and 10,000, and relays Ewell's about 900 at Harris Farm.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Humphreys' Union totals end on May 19–20 and exclude the cavalry; his Confederate figure is an inference.

open_questions: Grant's and Lee's reports, Hancock's, Warren's, Wright's, Burnside's, Ewell's and other corps reports, the compiled returns, Meade's casualty inclosure (garbled) and Humphreys' Chapter III narrative of May 9–11 and 12 (pp.62–92, 93–104, not read) remain deferred. The May 21 rear-guard action is in the frozen interval but only Meade's sentence on it was read.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan, and it shares headquarters papers with Meade's and Sheridan's reports. Meade's, Sheridan's, Hampton's, Butler's and Wild's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Parts 1 and 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
